{16–19} When Jibril (Gabriel) came to the Prophet (ﷺ) with the revelation and began reciting it to him, the Prophet (ﷺ), out of eagerness, would hasten ahead of him before he had finished, reciting along with Jibril's recitation. So Allah forbade him from doing that and said: ﴿Do not move your tongue with it to hasten it.﴾ And in another place He said: ﴿And do not hasten with the Qur'an before its revelation to you has been completed.﴾

Then Allah, may He be exalted, guaranteed to him that it would certainly be preserved for him, that he would recite it, and that Allah would gather it in his breast, so He said: ﴿Indeed, upon Us is its collection and its recitation.﴾ The eagerness that was in your heart was prompted only by fear of losing it and forgetting it. But when Allah has guaranteed it to you, there is no reason for that. ﴿So when We have recited it, then follow its recitation.﴾ That is: when Jibril has finished what is revealed to you, then follow what he has recited and recite it. ﴿Then indeed upon Us is its clarification.﴾ That is: the clarification of its meanings. Thus He promised him the preservation of its wording and the preservation of its meanings, and this is the highest of guarantees. The Prophet (ﷺ) complied with the discipline of his Lord, so whenever Jibril recited the Qur'an to him after this, he would listen attentively, and when he had finished, he would recite it.

In this verse there is a lesson in seeking knowledge: the student should not rush ahead of the teacher before the teacher has finished the matter he has begun; once the teacher has finished, the student should ask about what is unclear to him. Likewise, if at the beginning of a speech there is something that calls for rejection or approval, one should not hasten to reject it or accept it before the speech is complete, so that one may discern what in it is truth or falsehood, and understand it in a way that enables him to speak about it correctly. And in it: just as the Prophet (ﷺ) explained to the community the wording of the revelation, so too he explained its meanings to them.

{20–21} That is: what caused you to be heedless of and turn away from God's admonition and reminder is that **you love the fleeting life** (al-ʿājilah), and you strive for what obtains it and for its pleasures and desires, preferring it over the Hereafter, so you leave off action for the Hereafter. This is because the world, its bounties and pleasures, is fleeting, and man is inclined to love what is immediate, while the Hereafter is delayed, and what is in it of lasting bliss is out of sight. Therefore you have been heedless of it and abandoned it, as though you had not been created for it, and as though this abode were the abode of permanence, in which the choicest of lives are expended and for which one strives night and day. By this the truth was turned upside down for you, and there resulted the loss that resulted. Had you preferred the Hereafter over the world and looked at the consequences with the gaze of a discerning, intelligent person, you would have prospered and gained a profit with no loss in it, and you would have achieved a success with no misery accompanying it.

{22–23} Then He mentioned what calls to preferring the Hereafter, by describing the state of its people and the differences among them. Concerning the recompense of those who prefer the Hereafter over the world, He said: **"Faces that Day will be radiant, looking toward their Lord."** That is: beautiful, splendid, having brightness and light, because of the bliss of hearts, the delight of souls, and the pleasure of spirits that they are in. **"Looking toward their Lord"**: that is, they look upon their Lord according to their ranks. Among them are those who see Him every day, morning and evening, and among them are those who see Him once every Friday. They enjoy gazing upon His noble face and His dazzling beauty, to which nothing is comparable. So when they see Him, they forget the bliss they are in, and there comes to them a pleasure and joy that cannot be expressed, and their faces become radiant, so they gain beauty upon their beauty. We ask Almighty God to make us among them.

Therefore their faces have changed and become gloomy.

{26–30} Almighty God admonishes His servants by mentioning the dying person in the context of this discourse, and that when his soul reaches the collarbones (al-taraqi), which are the bones surrounding the hollow of the throat, then the distress intensifies and he seeks every means and cause through which he thinks healing and relief may be obtained. Hence He said: ﴿And it will be said, "Who can cure him?"﴾; that is, who will perform ruqyah (recitation of incantation) for him, from the word ruqyah, because their hopes have been cut off from the customary means, so they cling to divine means. But when the decree and destiny have been determined and have come, there is no averting them. ﴿And he will think that it was the parting﴾, that is, parting from the world. ﴿And the leg will be wound with the leg﴾; that is, the hardships will gather and intertwine, the matter will become great, the distress will become severe, and it is desired that the soul leave the body it has been accustomed to and has never ceased to be with, so that it is driven toward God Almighty to recompense it for its deeds and to hold it accountable for its actions. This admonition which God mentions drives hearts toward what is their salvation and restrains them from what is their destruction.

{31–33} But the obstinate one, to whom signs bring no benefit, continues steadfast in his error, disbelief, and stubbornness. ﴿So he neither believed﴾, that is, he did not believe in God, His angels, His books, His messengers, the Last Day, or divine decree, good and bad. ﴿Nor did he pray. But he denied and turned away﴾: he denied the truth in opposition to belief, and turned away from the command and prohibition. This while his heart is at rest, not fearing his Lord, rather ﴿he went to his family swaggering﴾; that is, nothing was on his mind.

{34–35} Then He threatened him by saying: ﴿Woe to you, and woe [again]. Then woe to you, and woe.﴾ These are words of threat, which He repeated to emphasize His threat.

{36–40} Then He reminded man of his original creation, saying: ﴿Does man think he will be left neglected?﴾; that is, left unattended, not commanded or forbidden, not rewarded or punished? This is a false assumption and a thought about God that is not befitting His wisdom. ﴿Was he not a drop of semen emitted? Then he was a clinging clot, and He created and proportioned [him]﴾: God created from it the living being and proportioned him; that is, perfected and made him sound. ﴿And made from him two sexes, male and female.﴾ ﴿Is not that One [who did this] able to give life to the dead?﴾: Yes, indeed He is Competent over all things.

The commentary on Surah Al-Qiyamah is complete. All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and may Allah send blessings and peace upon Muhammad (ﷺ).
